reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Mistaking os odontoideum for an acute fracture.
name: Anderson and D'Alonzo Classification of Odontoid Fractures

version.label: Anderson and D'Alonzo (1974), types I–III
version.detail: Grauer's subdivision of type II (IIA–IIC) is a later modification and is not combined.

intendedPopulation: Patients with odontoid fractures on CT.

options.label: Odontoid tip
options.detail: Oblique avulsion fracture through the tip of the dens.

options.label: Base of the dens
options.detail: Fracture at the junction of the dens and the body of C2.

options.label: Body of C2
options.detail: Fracture extending into the body of C2.

resultStates.label: Type I: odontoid tip
resultStates.summary: Oblique avulsion fracture through the tip of the dens.

resultStates.label: Type II: base of the dens
resultStates.summary: Fracture at the junction of the dens and the body of C2.

resultStates.label: Type III: body of c2
resultStates.summary: Fracture extending into the body of C2.

clinicalContext.text: Type II fractures have the highest non-union risk, especially with displacement, comminution or older age.

clinicalInsights.text: Displacement, angulation, comminution and age influence healing; describe them with the type.

limitations.text: Describes level only; displacement and stability are described separately.

limitations: Distinguishing low type II from shallow type III fractures varies between readers.

confounders.effect: Can mimic a type II fracture.

whatItDoesNotTellYou: Stability or the need for fixation on its own.

guideSections.what: Three types of odontoid fracture by level.
guideSections.howToPerform: Identify the fracture level on sagittal and coronal CT.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Used with displacement, age and comorbidity in management planning.

sources.citation: Anderson LD, D'Alonzo RT. Fractures of the odontoid process of the axis. J Bone Joint Surg Am. 1974;56(8):1663-1674.
